scope: G/Shift+G uses the selected brother's carried map through the original on-use script; development alpha

identification.detection: Prototype identity, independently of displayed names and the unused AutoMapProto class.

implementation: Search the selected actor through RecursiveContainerIterator on every accepted G press, including closed and nested bags; use the first map in iterator order.
Schedule MotionTask::useObject just like inventory double-click; original script conditions, explored map regions and selected-actor/world tracking remain intact.
Accept Shift+G; ignore Ctrl/Alt combinations, UI locks, modal dialogs, choice dialogue and held/dragged objects.
Report a missing carried map through the existing status line; items on the ground or carried by another brother do not grant access.
Add the fourteenth Hot Keys row using 13-pixel row spacing and height inside the unchanged 487 by 320 dialog; M continues to toggle music.
No new public API, configuration, command-line switch or game-data modification.

public_tests.new_checks: Injected SDL G, left/right Shift+G and Ctrl/Alt+G preserve key identity, case and modifier flags.

checks: G opens each of the three original maps from a closed Sack; SDL inventory double-click opens that same map and renders an identical map panel for each brother.
While the original on-use script is executing, its directObject equals the first recursively carried map and its enactor equals the selected brother.
Map track position equals the selected actor position; active map world matches the actor world; unexplored-map cheat mode remains off.
Shift+G opens a map placed directly in inventory. G also works through two closed nested bags and when multiple maps are carried.
Moving Julian's map onto the ground or into Philip's bag denies Julian access; the missing-map status message renders. Selecting Philip then uses his first carried map.
Repeated G, actor selection, M and O inside the map are ignored; settings, party flags and inventory snapshots remain unchanged during each modal opening.
Escape and the original close button restore the prior window. G over an open physical container followed by Escape closes only the map; a second Escape closes its parent.
Ctrl+G, Alt+G, UI lock, held-object state with a map still available, and a held mouse button block activation. Releasing the item/button permits opening again.
Options, Hot Keys and dialogue choices ignore G. Both Options layouts retain readable fourteen-row help without scrolling.
Fixtures restore all original inventory locations and flags; the deliberate ground fixture restores visibility flags set by the original renderer.
Earlier keypad, save/load, speech preference/restart, music, document cursor/wheel and container Escape regressions continue to pass.
integration.pixel_comparison: Compare the original map panel above local y=275; exclude the controls and translucent bottom shadow, whose background differs when a Sack is open.
integration.simulation: Nonmodal test frames retain normal simulation and ambient timing. Actor following and ambient RNG may advance between openings; each map tracks its actual selected actor.

memory.environment: Executed outside the sandbox to permit thread inspection

windows.build: Zig cross-build, Windows x64 Release, SDL 3.4.18
windows.execution: Native Windows processes from the preflight complete ZIP, using bundled-data discovery from an unrelated working directory

historical_reports: Unchanged from the 0.1.11 source ZIP; existing captures and checkpoints were preserved.

packages.validation: Final archives preserve the executable and SDL library tested in the preflight complete ZIP; the eight-file allowlist and original input hashes are unchanged.

limitations: Injected SDL input without a new physical-keyboard or mouse hardware check.
The original save places all three brothers in one world; another world and all scripted map conditions were not separately exercised.
The open-parent regression uses an original-data Sack, which shares ContainerWindow with chests.
The existing inventory double-click mouse-release path may repaint underlying bag controls over the map; this release preserves that path and tests map pixel parity before that release.
No new macOS execution, actual-device audio listening check or complete playthrough.
